headline: PAGASA: LPA Inside PAR May Become 'Pilandok' and Strengthen Habagat Rains
seoTitle: LPA May Become Pilandok, Strengthen Habagat | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA is monitoring an LPA inside PAR about 1,030 km east of Northern Luzon that may become a tropical depression and strengthen Habagat rains.
deck: The disturbance entered PAR early Thursday and may develop into a tropical depression within 48 hours, while the southwest monsoon continues to bring rain to Luzon and western Visayas.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PAGASA was monitoring a low-pressure area that entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility at around 2 a.m. Thursday and was estimated at about 1,030 kilometers east of Northern Luzon at 3 a.m.
Weather specialists said the disturbance may develop into a tropical depression within 48 hours. If it becomes a tropical cyclone while inside PAR, it will be given the local name Pilandok.

sections.heading: Habagat remains the immediate hazard
paragraphs: The southwest monsoon continued to affect Luzon and the western section of the Visayas. PAGASA forecast occasional rains over Zambales and Occidental Mindoro and scattered rains and thunderstorms across Metro Manila and several other parts of Luzon and western Visayas.

Moderate to heavy rain or severe thunderstorms can trigger flash floods and landslides in susceptible communities, while moderate to rough coastal waters were forecast over Luzon and the western Visayas.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The LPA is not yet a tropical cyclone. Development probabilities and tracks can change from one forecast cycle to the next, and hazardous monsoon rain can occur even without a direct landfall by the developing system.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Parts of Luzon remain vulnerable after repeated monsoon rain. A developing circulation east of the country can alter moisture flow and increase rainfall risk, making current local warnings more important than the eventual storm name.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: PAGASA will monitor whether the LPA organizes into a tropical depression and how strongly it interacts with the southwest monsoon. Residents should follow the latest rainfall, thunderstorm, flood and marine advisories as conditions evolve.
